summary: Frontend-only verification of the follow-up calendar fix: tapping the TRAINING-row workout card and 'SCHEDULED BY YOU' row card should navigate directly to Today's Training, while drag-to-reschedule and the day-header/SelectedDayPanel flows must keep working. Tested on demo@roujaune.app at 1600x1000 (wide/tablet layout). 4 of 5 scenarios PASSED. Found 1 bug: tapping a TRAINING-row card on a REST day does not select the day (right panel doesn't update) even though it correctly avoids navigating.

ui_bugs.component: DraggableSession (src/components/calendar.tsx) used by the TRAINING row
ui_bugs.issue: Tapping a TRAINING-row card for a REST day (e.g. 'Full Recovery') does nothing at all — it neither navigates (correct) NOR selects the day / updates the right-side SelectedDayPanel (incorrect, per spec it should still select the day). Verified reproducibly: clicked exact center of the card container (mouse.click and locator.click(force=True) both tried) on THU 'Full Recovery' — URL stayed on /calendar (good) but SelectedDayPanel kept showing Monday's session instead of updating to Thursday. By contrast, tapping the DAY-HEADER for the same rest day correctly updates the panel to Thursday. Root cause: DraggableSession receives `enabled={d.cycling.status !== 'rest'}` which is passed only to the Pan gesture (`Gesture.Pan().enabled(enabled)`), while the Tap gesture has no `.enabled()` call and should still fire onSelect via `Gesture.Exclusive(pan, tap)`. On web, Gesture.Exclusive() with one member's `.enabled(false)` appears to break tap recognition for the whole exclusive composition instead of falling through to the sibling Tap gesture, so onSelect never fires for rest-day cards.

action_items: Fix DraggableSession so the Tap gesture (onSelect) still fires for rest-day/disabled cards even though the Pan (drag) gesture is disabled. Suggested approach: don't disable Pan via .enabled(false) at the Gesture.Exclusive() composition level; instead keep pan built the same way but guard inside onDrop/enabled logic higher up, OR restructure to Gesture.Race(tap, pan) with pan requiring the long-press activation so tap always has a chance to win on a quick release regardless of the enabled flag, OR simply pass enabled into a wrapping condition so DraggableSession renders a plain Pressable (tap-only, no GestureDetector) when enabled=false instead of composing with a disabled Pan.
Retest after fix: tap a rest-day TRAINING card and confirm the right-side panel updates to that day while still not navigating.
critical_code_review_comments: goToWorkout() helper in app/calendar.tsx correctly centralizes the rest/empty-session guard (isRestRide check) and is consistently reused across day-header tap, training-card tap, scheduled-by-you card tap, SelectedDayPanel 'View Workout', and DayDetail modal 'View workout' buttons — good DRY practice.

TRAINING-row card tap-to-navigate works correctly for real cycling sessions: verified 'Pedal Stroke Drills' (Wed) navigates directly to /training with correct title/duration/zone/tss (50 min, Z2, 35 TSS), no intermediate popup.

SCHEDULED BY YOU row card tap-to-navigate works correctly: tapping 'Welcome Ride' card navigated directly to /training with workoutId=ctr-ride-1 and correct title/duration/tss; the separate small 'x' remove button (scheduled-remove-{id}) correctly removes the workout without navigating (confirmed via toast 'Removed Welcome Ride' and scheduled row becoming empty), confirming tap and remove-button gestures are properly isolated.

Drag-to-reschedule gesture (long-press ~300ms then drag) still works and did not break from the tap changes: dragging 'Pedal Stroke Drills' triggered the 'Alberto is reviewing your change' dialog with a contextual message ('Stacking those drills on Friday is fine, but we must keep the primer intensity very low.'), and Confirm/Cancel buttons are present and functional — confirms Gesture.Exclusive(pan, tap) correctly keeps drag and tap independent for enabled (non-rest) cards.

Day-header tap-to-navigate (previous iteration's fix) regression-verified still correct: cycling days navigate directly, rest days (THU 'Full Recovery') correctly open the DayDetail popup AND correctly update the SelectedDayPanel to that day — this is the correct behavior that the TRAINING-row card's rest-day tap should also achieve but currently doesn't.
SelectedDayPanel 'View Workout' button regression-verified working in wide/tablet layout — navigates to /training with the selected day's correct session data.

context_for_next_testing_agent: 4/5 acceptance scenarios passed cleanly: (1) TRAINING-row card tap on a real cycling day navigates directly to Today's Training with correct data — PASS. (2) TRAINING-row card tap on a rest day does NOT navigate — PASS, but it ALSO fails to select the day/update the right panel, which the spec says it should do — this is the one bug to fix. (3) Drag-to-reschedule (long-press + drag) still triggers the Alberto review dialog correctly and tap/drag gestures remain independent — PASS. (4) SCHEDULED BY YOU row card tap navigates directly and the 'x' remove button works independently without navigating — PASS. (5) Regression: day-header tap-to-navigate and DayDetail popup for rest days, plus SelectedDayPanel 'View Workout' button, all still work correctly — PASS. IMPORTANT TESTING NOTE for future agents: the FOCUS row (above TRAINING row) displays the exact same title text as the TRAINING-row card below it (e.g. both show 'Pedal Stroke Drills') — when using Playwright, select by testID (training-{id}) or the card's own bounding box, NOT by page.get_by_text(title) which can match the FOCUS row label instead and produce false test failures.
rca_of_issue: Bug: rest-day TRAINING card tap does nothing. In src/components/calendar.tsx, DraggableSession composes `Gesture.Exclusive(pan, tap)` where `pan = Gesture.Pan().enabled(enabled)` and enabled=false is passed for rest days (from calendar.tsx: `<DraggableSession enabled={d.cycling.status !== 'rest'} ...>`). The Tap gesture itself has no explicit `.enabled()` call, so in principle it should still recognize taps and call onSelect via runOnJS. However, on the web renderer, an Exclusive gesture group containing a disabled member does not appear to correctly hand off recognition to its sibling — the whole GestureDetector for that card stops responding to pointer events when the Pan gesture inside the Exclusive composition is disabled. Verified via direct mouse click at the card's exact bounding-box center (multiple methods: page.mouse.click, locator.click(force=True)) — no state change on /calendar (SelectedDayPanel remained on the previously-selected day) for the rest-day card, while the same click mechanics worked correctly for a non-rest TRAINING card (navigated) and for the day-header Pressable (selected + opened popup) on the same rest day.
